title: A Recipe for the Tryouts
premise: Ansel Almeida, a nonbinary statistician at Hollow Creek High, has quietly proven the school board rigs athletic eligibility for star players whose families donate — but exposing it means destroying the team that's been their only refuge. When the school's legendary ghost begins leaving notes in ink that shouldn't exist, each one naming students the board has wronged, Ansel realizes someone alive is using the legend as cover for justice. As prom approaches and the notes escalate toward public exposure, Ansel must choose between protecting their scholarship future and burning the institution down. The ghost turns out to be a janitor whose own child was erased from school records years ago; together they force the truth into the open at prom, and Ansel learns justice sometimes requires becoming the thing the rules fear.
about_author: Coral Whitlock is a former high school math tutor who spent three years collecting rumors about her own alma mater's eligibility scandals before writing fiction about them. She lives in a small town where everyone still believes the gym is haunted.

chapters.title: The Arithmetic of Waiting
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Opening day of senior spring: Ansel runs stats for the basketball team, privately tracking how benchwarmer Marcus Reyes got eligible despite failing two classes. Ansel counts down to graduation, numb and dutiful. Emotional beat: quiet resentment disguised as competence.

chapters.title: Note One
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. A note appears in Ansel's stat binder: 'You already know, Ansel Almeida. Why haven't you said?' The ink shimmers wrong under fluorescent light — too dark, like dried blood mixed with glitter. No handwriting matches any teacher's. Beat: fear sharpening into curiosity.

chapters.title: The Legend of Room 114
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, with best friend Priya. They research the ghost story: a student who died in 1987 after being declared academically ineligible mid-season, erased from yearbooks. Priya thinks it's a prank targeting Ansel specifically. Beat: the comfort of shared conspiracy.

chapters.title: Eligibility Is a Kindness
chapters.summary: Coach Danvers' POV. Coach defends the 'flexible' eligibility system to the athletic director, believing he's protecting kids from bureaucratic cruelty, blind to the donation ledger attached to every exception. Beat: complicity dressed as compassion.

chapters.title: Notes for the Wronged
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. More notes appear — in locked classrooms, inside sealed trophy cases — each addressed to a different student the board failed: a girl cut from track, a boy denied tutoring funds. Ansel starts a private spreadsheet connecting them all to board minutes. Beat: dread becoming purpose.

chapters.title: Marcus
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Marcus knows his eligibility was bought by his father's checkbook and hates carrying it. He finds a note addressed to him and burns it, terrified. He and Ansel circle each other, both holding halves of the same secret. Beat: shame and isolation.

chapters.title: The Board Meets in Closed Session
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel sneaks into the district office after hours hunting records and finds a 2019 file stamped DESTROY — the same date as a fire in the archive room. Someone else was there first; a flashlight beam sweeps the hall. Beat: hunter realizing they're hunted.

chapters.title: Ink That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Chemistry lab analysis of a recovered note: the pigment matches no commercial ink and contains trace compounds discontinued decades ago. Priya, a skeptic, starts believing despite herself. Beat: wonder cracking open cynicism.

chapters.title: Prom Committee Politics
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Prom planning collides with investigation when Principal Voss assigns Ansel to 'manage the narrative' around recent incidents. Voss is charming, watchful, and clearly knows more than she says. Beat: the enemy offering a gilded leash.

chapters.title: What the Scholarship Costs
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel's full-ride depends on a recommendation letter from Voss. Going public means losing college. A late-night conversation with Mom, who sacrificed everything for Ansel's future, makes the stakes brutally personal. Beat: love against duty, first collision.

chapters.title: The Ghost in the Boiler Room
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Following a fresh note's still-wet ink, Ansel corners the writer: Ray Delgado, night custodian, father of Elena Delgado — a student removed from all records in 2019 after her family sued the board. Ray never left; he just became invisible. Beat: the myth given a human face.

chapters.title: Elena
chapters.summary: Ray's POV, in flashback. 2019: Elena discovered the eligibility ledger, reported it, and was systematically discredited until she transferred away in disgrace. The board buried the lawsuit; the archive fire destroyed the evidence. Ray stayed to wait them out. Beat: grief transmuted into patience.

chapters.title: Partnership of the Damned
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel and Ray form an uneasy alliance: Ansel brings data and access, Ray brings thirty years of keys and knowledge of every hidden space in the building. First joint operation: photographing the surviving duplicate ledger in the sub-basement. Beat: hope with teeth.

chapters.title: Voss Closes In
chapters.summary: Principal Voss's POV. Voss identifies a pattern in the incidents and suspects an insider. She offers Ansel a deal — immunity for names — revealing she's not protecting the board but her own signature on the 2019 settlement. Beat: corruption wearing a helpful smile.

chapters.title: The Team Finds Out
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. The ledger leaks partially through the team group chat. Players turn on each other; Marcus, exposed as a bought eligibility, is ostracized. He comes to Ansel not for forgiveness but to testify. Beat: guilt choosing a side at last.

chapters.title: Locked Doors
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Voss suspends Ansel pending 'investigation,' confiscates their laptop, and changes the locks on the sub-basement. The evidence copies are safe, but the prom deadline looms — after graduation, jurisdiction shifts and the board buries everything permanently. Beat: the walls tightening.

chapters.title: Every Key Ray Ever Cut
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya organizes the resistance: students distribute printed ledger pages, the track team walks out, and Ray's master key ring opens the AV booth above the gymnasium. The plan forms: hijack prom's big screen. Beat: solidarity igniting.

chapters.title: The Night Before Prom
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel and Ray rehearse in the empty gym. Ray confesses he almost gave up last year; Ansel admits they almost took the deal. Voss discovers the AV booth plan via a planted rumor and prepares a countermove. Beat: calm before the storm, tenderness between allies.

chapters.title: Prom
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Under the disco lights, Voss announces Ansel's expulsion live — then the screens flicker and the ledger appears, page by page, narrated by Marcus over the microphone. The gym erupts. Board members attending as chaperones try to flee past a wall of students filming everything. Beat: catharsis, chaos, courage.

chapters.title: Aftermath in Fluorescent Light
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs braided. State investigators arrive within the week; Voss resigns citing health; Coach Danvers, shattered, cooperates fully. Marcus's eligibility is voided but his testimony earns him amnesty and unexpected respect. Beat: justice arriving messy but real.

chapters.title: Room 114, Repainted
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The board restores Elena Delgado's name to the records and dedicates a plaque. Ray retires, leaving Ansel his ring of keys as a joke and a blessing. Ansel's suspension is reversed; the scholarship is gone, but a journalism program offer arrives, unsolicited. Beat: mourning what was lost, honoring what was built.

chapters.title: A Recipe for the Tryouts
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, epilogue. At next year's tryouts, Ansel sits at the scorer's table as a credentialed observer for the district's new oversight committee. A fresh note waits in the binder — same impossible ink, different handwriting: 'Your turn.' Ansel smiles and picks up the pen. Beat: legacy passed forward, the cycle broken and renewed.
